cards.explanation: The answer is out of the whirlwind. Job 38:1 says the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind. After all those chapters of waiting for a reply, it arrives in the middle of a storm wind. I think Job stops talking and listens.

The answer is False. The text says Job's words obscure the LORD's counsel, which means they make it harder to see (Job 38:2). Words without knowledge don't clear anything up, friends. It's like pointing at a map with a very confident finger and a very wrong idea of where you are.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will question you, and you shall inform Me.” The roles flip. Job had said he wanted to speak to the Almighty and argue his case with God (Job 13:3), and now the LORD is the One asking, and Job is the one who has to answer.

The answer is building. Measurements, a measuring line, foundations and a cornerstone are all words from putting up a building. The LORD asks who fixed the earth's measurements and who stretched a measuring line across it (Job 38:5). Then He asks who laid its cornerstone. Picture a construction site with the whole earth on it.

The answer is shouting for joy. Job 38:7 says the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy. That's a celebration, and everybody is in on it. Job wasn't there for it, and that's the LORD's point. The stars sing, the sons of God shout, and the cornerstone goes down.

The answer is that He fixes its boundaries. The LORD says He fixed the sea's boundaries and set in place its bars and doors (Job 38:10). The sea bursts out, and it gets a limit. Bars and doors are things you put on a space to keep something where it belongs. It's like putting a fence around a very big, very loud dog.

The answer is True. The LORD speaks right to the sea. He declares, “You may come this far, but no farther…” (Job 38:11). Then He tells the proud waves they must stop. Most of us can't get a shopping cart to stop where we want, and here's the whole sea with a limit.

The answer is to the vents of the sea. The LORD asks, “Have you journeyed to the vents of the sea…” (Job 38:16). It's a question about a trip down to the deep places of the sea. Friends, I once thought the back of a junk drawer was far down.

The answer is True. The LORD asks, “Have the gates of death been revealed to you?” (Job 38:17). The next question asks it again with the shadow of death. This is a heavy place to go, so I'll just say it plainly: the LORD is asking whether Job has seen these gates.

The answer is home. The LORD asks, “Where is the way to the home of light?” (Job 38:19). Then He asks about the paths to darkness's home (Job 38:20). Light and darkness are each pictured with a place to go home to. I think that's a pretty picture, like both of them have a porch.

The answer is that Job wasn't around back then. The LORD already asked, “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?” (Job 38:4). Now He says, “Surely you know, for you were already born!” I think it's a pointed line, friends. Job wasn't there for the foundations.

The answer is False. The LORD says He holds the snow and hail in reserve, and He names times of trouble and the day of war and battle (Job 38:23). So they aren't just falling wherever they please. Reserve means set aside and kept. It's like a stack of cookie boxes waiting by the door for the big day.

The answer is False. The LORD says He brings rain on a barren land, on a desert where no man lives (Job 38:26). Then He says it makes the parched wasteland sprout with tender grass (Job 38:27). The rain falls on a desert where no man lives, friends.

The answer is being born. “Does the rain have a father? Who has begotten the drops of dew?” (Job 38:28). Then He asks from whose womb the ice emerges and who gives birth to the frost (Job 38:29). Father, womb and birth. The weather gets a baby album.

The answer is False. The LORD says the waters become hard as stone and the surface of the deep is frozen (Job 38:30). Water that hard sounds like something you'd stub a toe on. And He asks who gives birth to the frost from heaven (Job 38:29).

The answer is the laws of the heavens. The LORD asks, “Do you know the laws of the heavens?” (Job 38:33). Then He asks if Job can set their dominion over the earth. Laws for the sky is a big idea, bakers. I can barely get a cookie timer to behave.

The answer is True. The LORD asks, “Can you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are’?” (Job 38:35). Picture lightning checking in like an employee on Monday morning. Job can't call it, and that's the point of the question.

The answer is who put wisdom in the heart. The LORD asks, “Who has put wisdom in the heart or given understanding to the mind?” (Job 38:36). It comes right in the middle of the clouds and lightning. All that knowing the LORD keeps asking about had to come from somewhere.

The answer is rain. The LORD asks who can tilt the water jars of the heavens (Job 38:37). Tilt a jar of water over dust and you get rain on hard ground. The dust hardens into a mass, and the clods stick together (Job 38:38). I think it's a very good picture of a dry yard and a downpour.
